title: Tie-Dye Cotton Suits for Women: Bandhani vs Leheriya vs Shibori, Styling and Care
excerpt: Tie-dye cotton suits are soft, breathable and never exactly the same twice. How bandhani, leheriya and shibori differ, how to style a tie-dye suit and how to wash it so the colour lasts.
body:
Tie-dye is one of the oldest ways to pattern fabric. The cloth is tied, folded or bound before it goes into the dye, and the tied parts resist the colour. When the ties are opened, they leave white lines, dots or rings. A tie-dye cotton suit is light, breathable and a little different every time, which is why it works so well for everyday and summer wear.

*By the Bahe Kurtiz Styling Team, Jaipur.*

**Quick answer**

- Tie-dye = fabric tied or folded before dyeing, so parts stay undyed
- Bandhani, leheriya and shibori are all kinds of tie or resist dyeing
- Cotton tie-dye is soft, breathable and easy to wear all day
- No two pieces are exactly alike – small variations are normal
- Wash separately in cold water for the first few washes

## What is the difference between bandhani, leheriya and shibori?

| | Bandhani | Leheriya | Shibori |
|---|---|---|---|
| Where it comes from | Rajasthan and Gujarat | Rajasthan | Japan |
| How it is made | Tiny points of cloth tied tightly with thread | Cloth rolled diagonally and tied at intervals | Cloth folded, stitched, twisted or bound |
| What it looks like | Small dots, often in patterns | Wave-like diagonal stripes | Stripes, rings, grids and soft shapes |
| Mood | Festive, traditional | Bright, summery | Modern, artistic |

On Indian suits today, you will also see freer "tie-dye" patterns – bold bands, chevrons and ombre ends – that mix these ideas. Read more about dots in our guide to [what bandhani is and how to style it](/blog/what-is-bandhani-how-to-style-a-bandhani-anarkali/).

## Why choose a tie-dye cotton suit?

- **Comfort:** cotton breathes, so it stays comfortable through long, warm days.
- **Easy to style:** a printed suit with a plain bottom looks put-together with very little effort.
- **Every piece is unique:** the lines move slightly differently on every kurta and dupatta.
- **Works for many days:** office, college, a holiday or a relaxed festive lunch.

## How do I style a tie-dye suit?

### For office or college

Keep the rest simple. Small silver studs or light jhumkas, flat juttis or kolhapuris and a structured tote. Fold the dupatta over one shoulder so it stays out of the way.

### For a festive lunch or mehndi

Go bigger with jewellery – pearl or oxidised silver jhumkas, a stack of bangles and clear or metallic heels. Spread the dupatta across both arms to show the full pattern.

### For a holiday

Pair the kurta with the palazzo or pants and skip the dupatta for an easy, breezy look. Add sunglasses, a straw bag and flat sandals.

### Matching colours

Let the tie-dye be the star. Pick jewellery and shoes in silver, white, nude or one colour already in the print – for a pink and grey set, grey or silver works best.

## How do I wash tie-dye cotton so the colour lasts?

- Wash separately in cold water for the first few washes – tie-dye can bleed a little at first.
- Use a mild detergent. Do not bleach or soak.
- Turn it inside out and dry it in the shade, away from direct sun.
- Iron on medium heat, on the reverse side.

## Frequently asked questions

**Does tie-dye fade?**
All dyed cotton softens a little over time. Washing in cold water and drying in the shade keeps the colour bright for longer.

**Why does my tie-dye look slightly different from the photo?**
Tie-dye is made by tying the fabric before dyeing, so the lines and shades vary from piece to piece. Screens also show colour a little differently.

**Is tie-dye good for summer?**
Yes – cotton tie-dye is light and breathable, perfect for warm days.

**Is bandhani the same as tie-dye?**
Bandhani is one type of tie-dye, made by tying tiny points of fabric to create dots.
